notes:
Summary:
- Amberfield Risk Analytics evaluating Redwood Dedicated for productionizing claims-extract + fraud reranking pipeline and a policy-assistant chat for call center agents. Primary driver: predictable throughput for peak processing windows and tight p95 latency for live agent assist.

POC scope (what we agreed):
- Dedicated pool sizing options: compare 4x H100 vs 8x A100 80GB, with option to burst to additional reserved capacity for month-end peaks.
- Performance targets: 120 sustained req/s for policy-retrieval + chat (avg payload ~450 tokens), p95 generation latency target <= 220ms, end-to-end agent assist (incl network + routing) <= 400ms. Throughput guarantee conversation: want commit on baseline throughput and clearly defined backoff behavior.
- Soak tests: 48-hour soak at 80% of planned peak, plus 2-hour stress ramp to 150% for failure mode observation.
- Load tests: synthetic workload + recorded production replay (anonymized) — target 10k concurrent KV-cached sessions over 1h window.
- Quality checks: regression tests on 6 representative prompts (see below) to ensure quantized/fast variants don't regress.

Representative prompts (for benchmarking):
1) "Claim summary: extract injured party, policy id, incident date, short summary" (~35 tokens input, 180 tokens output)
2) "Policy retrieval: given agent query + 3 doc refs, return most relevant clause and confidence score" (~90 tokens input, 60 tokens output)
3) "Fraud rerank: rerank 50 candidate explanations by likelihood" (batch reranking workload, latency focus)
4) "Agent microchat: follow-up Q+A for claims adjudication, multi-turn, KV cache warm" (~turns 3-7)
5) "Sanitized call transcript summarization, TL;DR + key action items" (~500 tokens input, 120 token summary)
6) "Policy update diffing: given old+new policy text, list semantic changes" (long-context workload)

Tests executed so far / timeline (bullets):
- 2026-01-15: Intro call (AE+SE) — collected initial qps/latency targets and regulatory list (SAML, residency).
- 2026-01-22: Security questionnaire shared; infra team requested SOC2 report and KMS integration doc (linked).
- 2026-02-05: Architecture review with infra; confirmed VPC peering + private control plane acceptable.
- 2026-02-18: POC kickoff meeting (Fireflies ff_20260218_poc_kickoff) — agreed on dataset subset and representative prompt set.
- 2026-02-25: Baseline dry-run on 2x A100 nodes (synthetic) — observed p95 generation ~360ms (unoptimized).
- 2026-03-01: First dedicated cluster (2x H100) load test: sustained 60 req/s, p95 gen 180–220ms with KV cache warm, observed GPU mem headroom ~25%. Jira INF-4211 opened for kernel tuning request.
- 2026-03-03: Candidate quantized model built for cost run; initial quality checks show minor tokenization differences on policy-diff prompt.
- 2026-03-04: Security signoff partial: legal needs residency addendum; engineering cleared network flow.

Initial POC findings / observations (shorthand):
- H100 cluster hits p95 target with KV cache warmed; A100 config needs batching tweaks to hit latency target at same throughput.
- Batching policy: small batch sizes (4–8) + adaptive latency SLO enforcement performs better for chat use-case.
- Prefix/KV cache yields 30–45% cost savings for chat paths where session context re-used.
- Soak concern: observed small memory leak in custom kernel path under sustained high-concurrency -> SE note submitted to infra team (INF-4211).
- SLA discussion: customer expects an explicit throughput floor in contract (e.g., 100 req/s sustained) with credits if not met; Redwood proposal to offer reserved baseline + burst pool and runbook for mitigation.

Open action items (short):
- Deliver 48h soak run results + step-down charts (SE to produce; due 2026-03-10).
- Legal to draft residency clause for EU/NA split (customer wants EU data residency for EU customers).
- Redwood infra to propose final SKU mix (A100 vs H100) and cost delta per month.
- Product to propose explicit SLO wording for p95, 99, and availability with credit formulas.
- Schedule procurement kickoff w/ Amberfield finance (requested week of 2026-03-15).

Quotes / customer color: 
- "We need predictable throughput the week our partners process batch claims; variability is our biggest risk." — VP Eng
- CTO note: wants single-tenant control plane + audit log retention 7 years for compliance review.

Risk / blockers (details):
- Procurement: long vendor review cycles (legal + infosec).
- Residency/retention: exact language for EU residency and retention windows (48h vs 7y) still under negotiation.
- SKU approval: Finance prefers A100 pricing but Eng favors H100 headroom; procurement awaiting final pricing.

Links & artifacts referenced:
- Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_amberfield-poc (contains workload replay, prompts, pricing deck)
- Fireflies: ff_20260301_amberfield_kickoff (test call transcript)
- Jira: INF-4211 (kernel/soak issue)
- Gmail thread: thread_9876543210 (pricing negotiation)

Recommended Redwood playbook items (for AE/SE):
- Prepare SKU comparison doc (cost/throughput curves) with annotated failover policies.
- Draft SLO language + credit table to present to customer legal next week.
- Prioritize fix for kernel leak and include mitigation steps in POC report.
